consensus_summary: The Ancient of Days is the eternal God, usually identified as God the Father, portrayed as the enthroned sovereign Judge; advanced age signifies eternity, wisdom, and primordial authority.
book_summary: The Ancient of Days is the venerable divine One who stands at the origin and head of Daniel’s calendrical cycle, from whose initiating day the month, year, and age advance.
consensus_core_identification: The eternal God portrayed as the ancient, sovereign heavenly Judge.
book_core_identification: The same venerable divine figure, specifically identified as the origin and governing head of a calendrical progression of days and larger periods.
boundary_disagreement: The book retains the divine referent but reclassifies the age-language as denoting a specific calendrical office, not merely divine antiquity or pre-existence. It therefore restricts the title’s intended symbolism to God’s position at the head of Daniel’s temporal cycle.
material_contradiction: There is no contradiction over the figure’s divine identity. The material disagreement concerns what “advanced in days” signifies: the consensus treats it as imagery of eternity and judicial authority without a calendar office, whereas the book makes calendrical origin and advancement integral to the title.
rationale: Because the book preserves the consensus’s central referent—the divine Ancient of Days—but materially specifies a calendrical role absent from and expressly contrasted with the common view, the relationship is REFINED rather than MATCH or DIVERGENT. The same three Daniel occurrences are retained, but their symbolism is partially reclassified.
strongest_objection: Daniel 7:9–22 explicitly presents an enthroned judicial figure but does not explicitly state that he occupies the first day of a cycle or that months, years, and ages advance from him. Psalm 93:2 and Isaiah 43:13 support primordial existence, yet do not by themselves establish the proposed calendar office.
